This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with real reports of players. Then it explains the idea behind them.
It ends with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on
this page has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary frame-rate frame-time stutter one-percent-low thermal-throttling frame-rate-cap compatibility api-level graphics-api compatibility-matrix release-notes reliable-source >}}

## 14.1 Measuring performance

- **Frame time:** the time of one frame; 60 fps ≈ 16.7 ms, 30 fps ≈ 33.3 ms
  (1000 ms ÷ fps).
- **Average fps** over a whole race; the **1 % low**: the slowest 1 % of the
  frames. A low 1 % low means **stutters** (jerks).
- Test as long as players play: a hot chip slows down (**thermal
  throttling**, lecture 3). A **frame-rate cap** or lower settings keep the
  game steady.
- Star Garden: 59 fps on average, but one 70 ms frame every 10 seconds (a
  cloud save) → a stutter.

![Frame times of one race.](images/frame-times.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A high average with many stutters feels worse than a steady 30 fps.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Frame times"}
Compute the frame time of 30, 60 and 120 fps (1000 ms ÷ fps). A frame takes
50 ms: which frame rate would that be if all frames took that long?

::: {.check}
30 fps: ≈ 33.3 ms. 60 fps: ≈ 16.7 ms. 120 fps: ≈ 8.3 ms. A 50 ms frame:
1000 ÷ 50 = 20 fps. One such frame in a 60 fps race is a stutter.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Measures"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="100 ms|0 ms"}
What is the frame time at 60 fps?
:   about 16.7 ms

    Why: 1000 ms ÷ 60 ≈ 16.7 ms.

Which number shows the stutters?
:   the 1 % low

    Why: It is the frame rate of the slowest frames.

What is a single 50 ms frame in a 60 fps race?
:   a stutter

    Why: It is three times longer than the other frames.

A phone is hot after 15 minutes and slows down. What is it?
:   thermal throttling

    Why: A hot chip lowers its speed to protect itself.
:::
:::

## 14.2 Compatibility

- **Minimum OS version:** a build for Android 11 (API 30) cannot start on
  Android 8.
- **Graphics API** (Vulkan, OpenGL ES, Metal): an old GPU without Vulkan
  shows a black screen if the build has no other path.
- **Screen shapes:** 20:9 with a notch, 16:9, 4:3 tablets: anchor the menus
  in the **safe area**.
- A **compatibility matrix** records each device and each check.

![A compatibility matrix.](images/compat-matrix.png){width=90%}

![One menu, three screen shapes.](images/aspect.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/compat-lab.html" poster="sims/compat-lab.png" title="Compatibility Lab: build 43 for every device" height="580" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Every older version and every graphics path adds testing: check how many
players really use them.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The matrix"}
In **Compatibility Lab**, make every row green. Write the cost of each
setting you changed.

::: {.check}
Minimum Android 8 (API 26): the game must be tested on Android 8 too, and
avoid newer features. Vulkan + OpenGL ES: a second graphics path to test.
Menu anchored to the safe area: one more layout check per screen shape.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Compatibility"}
Use Compatibility Lab. Choose the fix.

::: {.match extra="a bigger icon|a faster network"}
A crash at start on Android 8.
:   minimum Android 8 (API 26)

    Why: The build must be made for the oldest version it supports.

A black screen on a GPU without Vulkan.
:   add OpenGL ES 3

    Why: A second graphics path for old GPUs.

The Start button cut off on a tablet.
:   anchor the menu to the safe area

    Why: The layout must fit every screen shape.

What do all three fixes cost?
:   more testing

    Why: Each version, path and shape must be tested.
:::
:::

## 14.3 Following developments with reliable sources

- Read the **release notes** of new OS and engine versions: they list the
  changes that can break a game.
- **Reliable:** official documentation, release notes, benchmarks that
  explain their method, your own written tests.
- **Claims to check:** ads, forum rumours, undated posts, one video with
  one device.
- After an update, run the test plan again on an updated device.
- A video says "twice the frame rate on old phones": the release notes say
  only faster loading; Rami's own test confirms it.

![Where do performance facts come from?](images/sources.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A number from a video needs its source and date before it goes into a report.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A release note"}
Find the release notes of the newest Android or iOS version on the official
developer site. Write two changes that could affect a game, with the source
and the date.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "developer.android.com, Android 16 behaviour
changes (read on 30 October 2026): 1. on tablets the system can ignore a
game that locks the screen to portrait, so the game must also work in
landscape; 2. background work has new limits, so the cloud save in the
background must be tested again."

- ☐ An official page and the date you read it.
- ☐ Two changes, each with what it means for a game.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Sources"}
Choose the kind of source. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="a secret|a guess"}
The official release notes of an OS.
:   reliable

    Why: The maker writes what changed, with a date.

A forum post without tests.
:   a claim to check

    Why: No author, no data: test it first.

Your own test log with dates.
:   reliable

    Why: Written tests with dates can be repeated.

An undated video with one device.
:   a claim to check

    Why: One device and no date say little.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Performance Detective {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Players of **Pocket Quest** send **six reports**: a race that **jerks at
58 fps**; a **hot** phone that slows down after **15 minutes**; a **crash
on Android 8**; a **black screen** on an old phone; a **Start button cut
off** on a tablet; and a **forum claim** that an OS update makes every game
30 % faster.

{{< sim file="sims/perf-detective.html" poster="sims/perf-detective.png" title="Performance Detective: six player reports" kind="game" height="460" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The reports"}
Choose the cause or the fix.

::: {.match extra="a full storage|a slow network"}
The race jerks at 58 fps.
:   stutters: look at the 1 % low

    Why: The average hides the long frames.

Slower after 15 minutes, and the phone is hot.
:   thermal throttling

    Why: The hot chip slows down.

A black screen on an old phone.
:   no support for the graphics API

    Why: The old GPU has no Vulkan.

"Every game 30 % faster."
:   check the release notes and test

    Why: A forum claim needs an official source and a test.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Fixes (harder)"}
The hot phone, the Android 8 crash and the tablet. Choose the best fix.

::: {.match extra="a bigger battery|delete the tablet version"}
The phone gets hot and slows down in long races.
:   a 30 fps cap or lower settings

    Why: Less work per second keeps the chip cooler and the race steady.

The crash at start on Android 8.
:   build with minimum Android 8 and test on it

    Why: The build must support the oldest version it is offered on.

The Start button cut off on the tablet.
:   anchor the menu to the safe area

    Why: The layout fits every screen shape.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Measure frame times and the 1 % low, not only the average fps, in long
  tests on real devices.
- A frame-rate cap or lower settings keep a hot phone steady.
- Builds fail from the minimum OS version, the graphics API or the screen
  shape: keep a compatibility matrix.
- Follow platform changes in release notes and official documentation, and
  test after every update.
